_doc: Schema: see docs/reference/api-parity-ledger/SCHEMA.md — the one home for what
a row means. Do NOT copy it back here; issue 1095 is what that cost.

c:context_*.why: rcl splits initialization in two -- an `rcl_context_t` built from a separately-constructed `rcl_init_options_t` -- and threads the context through every entity's init. nano-ros collapses both into `nros_support_t`, which is rclc's `rclc_support_t` name and carries the RMW session INLINE (`_opaque[SESSION_OPAQUE_U64S]`, nros_generated.h:949). The constraint is no allocator: rcl's context hands out a heap `rcl_context_impl_t` and its accessors exist to reach into it, and there is nothing here for them to reach. The useful half lives on `nros_support_*`.

c:get_default_domain_id.why: rcl reads ROS_DOMAIN_ID from the environment at runtime. An embedded backend has no environment (RFC-0036, Domain ID), so the domain arrives through `nros_support_init`'s parameter over a documented ladder -- explicit argument, then hosted env, then the baked default -- with `NROS_DOMAIN_ID_INHERIT`/`NROS_DOMAIN_ID_EXPLICIT_ZERO` sentinels because plain 0 has to stay the UNSET marker (issues 0206/0227).

c:get_zero_initialized_context.why: there is no context type to zero-initialize. `nros_support_get_zero_initialized` is the same idiom on the type we do have.

c:init.why: `rcl_init(argc, argv, options, context)` is the layer BELOW rclc, and rclc's own examples do not call it -- they call `rclc_support_init`, which is what `nros_support_init` mirrors. Declining the lower layer is what makes the C API rclc-shaped rather than rcl-shaped.

c:init_options_*.why: the options half of the same collapse. `rcl_init_options_t` is built, mutated (set_domain_id), copied and finalised before rcl_init consumes it; ours are the two arguments `nros_support_init` takes. There is no `nros_init_options_t`: `nros_support_init(support, locator, domain_id)` takes as arguments the two values rcl's options would carry. CORRECTED 2026-09-04 (phase-417): the sweeping form of this claim -- "there is no runtime options object" -- is false one stage over. Seven ENTITY options structs ship and correlate `same` (see `c:node_options_*`); INIT is a stage that genuinely has none.

c:shutdown.why: as `rcl_init`: the rcl-layer counterpart. `nros_support_fini` is the rclc-shaped teardown.

c:support_get_zero_initialized.why: as `support_is_valid`: rcl's zero-init idiom applied to `nros_support_t`, which rclc does not provide for `rclc_support_t`.

c:support_init_named.why: `nros_support_init` plus a node name. RFC-0046 makes launch the authority on node identity, and an image that was told its name at boot should not have to re-derive it; rclc has no equivalent because a desktop node gets its name from argv.

c:support_init_rmw.why: `nros_support_init_named` plus a backend selector -- it names the RMW backend the session opens against. rclc/rclcpp have no counterpart because a ROS 2 desktop process selects its middleware with the `RMW_IMPLEMENTATION` environment variable, and an embedded image has no environment to read -- which is precisely how issue 1050 happened: the selector had an env rung and no baked one, so a PX4 module declaring `BACKENDS uorb` could not say so and the registry's first entry won. The hosted env rung (`$NROS_RMW`) still takes precedence, matching `RMW_IMPLEMENTATION`'s authority; this is the rung beneath it.

c:support_init_with_options.why: rclc's options-taking variant. Same constraint as `compile-time-options`: there is no `rcl_init_options_t` to pass.

c:support_is_valid.why: mirrors `rcl_context_is_valid` on the type we actually have. Counted as an extension rather than a rename because rclc -- the C reference -- ships no `rclc_support_is_valid`; we are adding to rclc, not renaming rcl.

c:support_state_t.why: an explicit lifecycle for the support object (uninitialised / initialised / finalised) so a double-init or a use-after-fini is a returned code rather than undefined behaviour. rcl relies on a zero-initialized struct plus `rcl_context_is_valid`; a device that cannot report a crash needs the state to be inspectable.

cpp:Context.why: rclcpp lets several contexts coexist so one process can host independent ROS graphs, and every entity holds a `Context::SharedPtr`. An image is ONE graph and has no allocator for a context registry, so `nros::init()` initialises the single global one and nothing carries a context pointer. The accessors (`get_rcl_context`, `get_sub_context`, `get_init_options`) exist to reach into that per-context state.

cpp:ContextAlreadyInitialized.why: an exception type, and the freestanding builds are -fno-exceptions (RFC-0018). Re-initialising returns `ErrorCode::AlreadyExists` through `nros::Result`.

cpp:InitOptions.why: the C++ face of `rcl_init_options_t`; see `c:init_options_*`. `auto_initialize_logging` and `use_default_domain_id` are runtime toggles for decisions taken at build time here (RFC-0045).

cpp:get_contexts.why: enumerates the process's contexts; there is exactly one and it is not a value you can hold. See `cpp:Context`.

envelope.text: every other ROS argument ABORTS the process naming it.

cpp:init.why:
ours is `init(const char* locator, uint8_t domain_id [, const char* node_name])`; rclcpp's is `init(int argc, char** argv, const InitOptions&, SignalHandlerOptions)`. Both take two arguments and share nothing else -- the correlator reports this as `arity-only` for that reason. Three constraints at once: no argv on a device (RFC-0045), no runtime options object, and no POSIX signals. What is left is the two things a device must actually be told, named directly.

phase-428 W6 (2026-09-06) — disposition, required because this row's SHAPE CORRESPONDS: the name exists on the ported surface and the correlator files it `same`, so nothing in a build says the contract differs. That is the class RFC-0089 exists for.

This is the case RFC-0089 Part I is written around, so the disposition is stated against the rule rather than summarised.

UPSTREAM'S CONTRACT: `rclcpp::init(int argc, char** argv, ...)` returns `void` and PARSES `--ros-args` — remaps and parameter overrides reach a process this way.

OURS: `packages/api/nros-cpp/include/nros/nros.hpp:415` — `inline void init(int argc, char const* const* argv)`, which does not parse argv. It scans it with `constexpr detail::argv_has_ros_args` (`:329`) and, if `--ros-args` is present, emits `NROS_RCLCPP_REFUSE_INIT_ARGV` and calls `std::abort()`. The zero-argument `init()` at `:427` is ADOPT outright. The native `nros::init(locator, domain_id)` described above is a different entry point and is unaffected.

HOW A USER FINDS OUT: a program with no ROS arguments is unaffected, because nothing was dropped. A program that passes them DIES IMMEDIATELY, naming the flag, instead of running for hours on a remap that was never applied.

WHY THIS IS NOT REFUSE-LOUD AT COMPILE TIME: whether argv carries `--ros-args` is a VALUE, not a type. A `static_assert` on the two-argument overload would reject every caller — including the common embedded one that forwards `main`'s argv and has no ROS arguments at all — and would make upstream's own tutorial `main` unportable. RFC-0089's requirement is LOUDNESS, and compile time is the earliest point loudness is available, not the only point it is permitted. The predicate is `constexpr` precisely so it is separately checkable: its cases are `static_assert`ed in the ordinary compile lane, rather than being observable only by a process that then dies.

phase-428 Q1 (2026-09-06): SITE, re-cited after the header moved -- the scan is `packages/api/nros-cpp/include/nros/nros.hpp:416`, the log is `NROS_ERROR("%s", NROS_RCLCPP_REFUSE_INIT_ARGV)` at `:420` (message `packages/api/nros-cpp/include/nros/log.hpp:194`) followed by `std::abort()`. Probe: `packages/api/nros-cpp/tests/compile/ros2_init_argv_refusal.cpp`, which `static_assert`s the predicate's cases including the two mutations that would silence it. The Rust twin is `rust:init_with_args`, now the same shape.

phase-467 Row 11, C++ half (2026-10-05) -- `rclcpp::init(argc, argv)` now HONOURS `--ros-args -r` instead of refusing `--ros-args` as such. It parses with the same code as Rust's `nros::Context::new` (`nros_node::ros_args::apply_ros_args`, through the new `nros_cpp_install_argv_remaps`), validates BEFORE the session opens, and installs the rules into the open executor as the FALLBACK beneath launch remaps. Every other ROS argument (`-p`, `--params-file`, `__node`, `--enclave`, the log flags, an unknown token) still aborts, naming it -- `void` return, so there is nowhere else to put it. The envelope moved with the text; the remaining bound is the refused set, which is RFC-0015 section 9's and RFC-0046's to lift. Held by the runtime probe `packages/api/nros-cpp/tests/compile/init_honours_ros_args.cpp` (`just check cpp`).

cpp:install_signal_handlers.why: no POSIX signal delivery on Zephyr, FreeRTOS or bare-metal. rclcpp installs a SIGINT handler so Ctrl-C shuts the context down; an image is stopped by its RTOS, a watchdog or a power rail.

cpp:on_shutdown.why: CLOSED as a gap by issue 0790: `nros::on_shutdown(cb, ctx)` now exists, so the names correspond and the row is arity-only rather than theirs-only. What still differs is the SIGNATURE, and the platform constraint is no allocator: rclcpp takes `std::function<void()>`, a heap allocation per callback, while a freestanding no-STL header takes a function pointer plus an opaque `context` and stores the pair in a fixed-capacity static table (`NROS_EXECUTOR_MAX_SHUTDOWN_CBS`, default 2). The `out` handle parameter is the third argument for the same reason rclcpp returns one -- so a callback can be removed -- but it is an out-param because this API does not throw and registration can fail with `Full`. The PRE-shutdown phase, which is the half a device actually needs, is `cpp:pre_shutdown` here and `cpp:Executor::add_pre_shutdown_callback` in exec.json.

cpp:pre_shutdown.why: `nros::pre_shutdown(cb, ctx)` -- the free-function spelling of the PRE-shutdown phase over the global executor, next to `nros::on_shutdown`. rclcpp has a free `rclcpp::on_shutdown` but no free pre-shutdown form; having only the post-teardown one as a free function would leave the half that matters on a device reachable only through the executor object. The phase itself is recorded on `cpp:Executor::add_pre_shutdown_callback` (exec.json). Issue 0790.

cpp:remove_on_shutdown_callback.why: Removal counterpart of `cpp:on_shutdown` over the global executor. rclcpp spells it `Context::remove_on_shutdown_callback`; we have no `Context`, so it sits beside the free `on_shutdown` it undoes. Issue 0790.

cpp:remove_pre_shutdown_callback.why: Removal counterpart of `cpp:pre_shutdown` over the global executor. rclcpp's removals live on `Context`, which we do not have; see `cpp:Context`. Issue 0790.

cpp:remove_ros_arguments.why:
argv filtering. On a device there is no argv: RFC-0045 resolves boot config from baked values and the board.

phase-467 Row 11 follow-through (2026-10-03) -- CORRECTED. "there is no argv" was the whole reason, and it stopped being true on a hosted build: since #1591 the RUST entries (`nros::init_with_args` / `nros::Context::new`) parse `--ros-args` and honour `-r`. The C++ surface still has nothing to strip -- `nros::init(argc, argv)` calls no parser and ABORTS on `--ros-args` (`NROS_RCLCPP_REFUSE_INIT_ARGV`, `packages/api/nros-cpp/include/nros/nros.hpp`), so a C++ caller never hands ROS arguments past `init` that this would remove. Stays `absent` until a C++ entry parses; the Rust parse already scopes `--ros-args ... --` itself, so the program's own arguments are never mistaken for ROS ones.

phase-467 Row 11, C++ half (2026-10-05) -- the sentence above went stale two days later: `nros::init(argc, argv)` no longer aborts on `--ros-args`, it honours `-r` and refuses the rest (see `cpp:init`). Still `absent`, and the reason is now the real one: rclcpp's `remove_ros_arguments` exists so a program can hand ITS OWN parser an argv without the ROS tokens. Our parse already scopes `--ros-args ... --` itself and ignores everything outside, so nothing upstream of a user's parser needs stripping; and a returned `std::vector<std::string>` has no freestanding spelling (RFC-0096). Adopt it when a user asks for it.

cpp:shutdown.why: phase-428 W6 remainder (2026-09-06) — ledgered because the correlator's return-type comparison became a VERDICT. `rclcpp::shutdown(context, reason)` returns `bool` — `true` when THIS call was the one that shut the context down, `false` when it was already down. Ours (`packages/api/nros-cpp/include/nros/node.hpp:181,1031`) returns `Result`. The widening is RFC-0018's and is LOUD for a discarded statement (`Result` is `[[nodiscard]]`), but note what changes for the ported idiom `if (rclcpp::shutdown()) { ... }`: upstream's `false` means "someone else already did it", an ORDINARY answer, while a falsy `Result` means an ERROR. A ported conditional keeps compiling and stops meaning the same thing. Recorded here rather than actioned because the shape is right — an error channel is required — and the fix, if one is wanted, is to make "already shut down" an `ok` rather than a failure. Sibling of `rclcpp::init` returning `void` upstream and `Result` here, which is RFC-0089 Part I's own worked example.

rust:Context.why:
phase-428 Q1 follow-through (2026-09-06) — `env` joined the measured feature set (`scripts/api_parity/extract_rust.py`, `NROS_FEATURES`), so this type is on the surface for the first time and correlates `same`; it read `theirs-only` before only because the extractor never compiled `src/init.rs`. The old text ("as `cpp:Context` ... neither is available to an image with no env and one session") described the invisible state and is history.

UPSTREAM'S CONTRACT: `rclrs::Context` (0.7.0, `rclrs/src/context.rs`) OWNS the rcl context — built from argv (`Context::new(args, options)`) or the environment (`from_env`, `default_from_env`), it parses `--ros-args`, answers `domain_id()` / `ok()`, and is the factory for executors (`create_executor`).

OURS (`packages/api/nros/src/init.rs`, by name): a plain value `{domain_id, locator, mode, rmw, source}` that the free functions `nros::init()` / `init_with_args` / `init_with_launch*` return, and whose one method `config(node_name)` (by name) materialises the `ExecutorConfig` a caller hands to `Executor::open`. It owns nothing and parses nothing: it is the resolved identity, read through the one hosted resolver (`nros::env::try_resolve_hosted`, issue 0687).

Disposition ADOPT-BOUNDED. The name carries the same identity (domain, middleware selection), and `ctx.domain_id` reads where `ctx.domain_id()` did; the envelope is that construction is the free `init*` family (the argv form REFUSES `--ros-args`, see `rust:init_with_args`); `Context::default_from_env()` is the one member that maps 1:1 onto ours, `nros::init()`, and its row is a `rename`, that the executor is opened INTO caller-owned storage from `ctx.config(name)` rather than allocated by the context (RFC-0045; no allocator), and that there is no `ok()` because the value has no shutdown state — liveness is the executor's. Each missing member has its own row below, because the type is `same` and a member gap inside a shipped type is argued on its own (`lookup`'s inheritance rule). The whole module is behind `env`, which requires `std`: an embedded image never compiles it, and its identity arrives through `BootConfig` instead.

phase-427 W9 (2026-09-07) — LANDED. The last sentence above is history: `init.rs` is out from behind `env`. `Context` (`packages/api/nros/src/init.rs`, by name) compiles on every target with `alloc` as its floor (`locator` and `rmw` are owned `String`s); the `env` feature gates only the process-environment reader and the argv/launch entries. The rclrs constructors exist under their names — `default_from_env` (`adopt`), `from_env` (`adopt-bounded`), hosted-only `new` (`adopt-bounded`) — each on its own row; freestanding, the first two resolve to `Context::baked()` (`rust:Context::baked`). Construction is no longer ONLY the free `init*` family; the envelope that remains is the executor being opened from `ctx.config(name)` (RFC-0045) and the absence of `ok()`.

issue 1637 (2026-10-05) — ENVELOPE WRITTEN, and one half CORRECTED. The type's rustdoc said nothing about the missing `ok()`. And the "executor opened INTO caller-owned storage from `ctx.config(name)` rather than allocated by the context" half above is stale: `Context::create_executor` (leaks an executor-lifetime backing, `alloc`) and `Context::create_executor_in` (caller storage) now exist, so the context IS the factory for executors, as rclrs's is. What remains bounded — no `ok()`, `domain_id` a field rather than a method, the context a resolved value rather than an rcl-context owner — is now on `Context`'s rustdoc.

rust:Context::baked.why:
phase-427 W9 (2026-09-07) — LANDED. `Context::baked() -> Result<Context, InitError>` (`packages/api/nros/src/init.rs:329`): the FREESTANDING constructor, from the constants baked into this crate at compile time — `option_env!("NROS_LOCATOR")` (unset or empty ⇒ empty ⇒ the linked backend's own default, issue 0330) and `option_env!("NROS_DOMAIN_ID")` (unset ⇒ 0; non-numeric ⇒ `EnvParseFailed`; above `DOMAIN_ID_MAX` ⇒ `DomainIdOutOfRange`). Mode `Client`, `rmw` empty, source `ContextSource::Baked`. This is what `default_from_env()` / `from_env()` resolve to when `env` is off, and it is the ONE `option_env!` site for the pair: the entry macros (`nros::zephyr_component_main!`, `packages/api/nros/src/lib.rs:953`; `nros::main!`'s Zephyr arm, `packages/core/nros-macros/src/main_macro.rs:1960`) used to carry their own copies and assemble an `ExecutorConfig` by hand — and the `main!` copy had lost the domain half (issue 0161's class), so a workspace Zephyr entry ran domain 0 whatever Kconfig said. Both call `Context::default_from_env()` now. The values reach THIS crate's build through `nros_zephyr_build::bake_nros_config()` in `packages/api/nros/build.rs:37` (Kconfig via `$DOTCONFIG`, the issue-0460 channel) or the process environment of a fixture build. The parse behind it, `from_baked(locator, domain)` (`:338`, `#[doc(hidden)]`), takes the two constants as arguments so a unit test covers every arm without a build environment (`init::baked_tests`). `with_locator_override` (`:364`) is the harness's `-testargs --nros-locator=<loc>` override on top (#166 / phase-286 W1), resolved in the entry because the `nros_runtime_locator_override` hook is an `extern "C"` only a Zephyr image defines.

No upstream counterpart: rclrs has one constructor family and a process environment on every target it supports; this is the RTOS half of `rust:Context::default_from_env`'s bounded adoption, and the reason that row can say `adopt`.

rust:Context::config.why:
phase-428 Q1 follow-through (2026-09-06) — `Context::config(&self, node_name) -> ExecutorConfig` (`packages/api/nros/src/init.rs:126`): the one method on our `Context`, turning the resolved identity into the config `Executor::open` takes, with the node name supplied at the call because one process can open several nodes on one identity. rclrs has no counterpart: its `Context` is passed to `create_node` / `create_executor` directly, because it owns the rcl context those consume. Ours owns nothing (see `rust:Context`), so the seam between identity and session is an explicit conversion. Borrowing (`ExecutorConfig<'a>` over `&'a self`) is what keeps the config heap-free.

phase-467 Row 11 (2026-10-03) -- REFUSES a context that carries `--ros-args` remaps. An `ExecutorConfig` has nowhere to put them, so the executor `Executor::open` builds from it would never see them -- the silent drop `init_with_args` exists to prevent. It panics naming `create_executor` / `create_executor_in`, which install them. A context without remaps -- every context not built from an argv that carried `-r` -- is unaffected (`config_is_unaffected_without_remaps`).

rust:Context::default_from_env.why:
phase-427 W9 (2026-09-07) — LANDED. `Context::default_from_env() -> Result<Context, InitError>` (`packages/api/nros/src/init.rs:253`) exists under the rclrs spelling. Same name, same observable contract on a hosted build: it IS `nros::init()` (`:424`), which stays as the C++-symmetric anchor (`rust:init`), and both read the process environment through the one hosted resolver.

Why a `divergence` and not a plain match: the PLATFORM CONSTRAINT is that a freestanding image has no process and no environment (RFC-0089 "Context and `init`, settled"). There the same function resolves to `Context::baked()` (`:329`, `rust:Context::baked`) — the constants `NROS_LOCATOR` / `NROS_DOMAIN_ID` baked into the crate's build, from Kconfig on Zephyr — and the source it reports is `ContextSource::Baked`. The semantics survive with the source moved from run time to build time ("the environment this image was built for or launched in"), which is what makes the disposition `adopt` rather than `adopt-bounded`: a ported `let ctx = Context::default_from_env()?;` compiles and does what it says on every target, and the ONLY thing bounded is where the values came from, stated on the type and on the `source` field. The error type differs (`InitError`, see `rust:RclrsError`), invisible under `?`.

History: filed `gap` + `absent` by the phase-428 Q1 follow-through, re-verdicted `rename` (to `nros::init()`) by the phase-428 closure, decided 2026-09-07 (RFC-0089) and landed here. Hosted tests: `init::ros_args_refusal_tests::default_from_env_is_init`; freestanding: `init::baked_tests::freestanding_default_from_env_is_the_bake` (`cargo test -p nros --no-default-features --features alloc --lib`).

rust:Context::from_env.why:
phase-427 W9 (2026-09-07) — LANDED. `Context::from_env(options: InitOptions) -> Result<Context, InitError>` (`packages/api/nros/src/init.rs`, by name): `default_from_env()` with the `InitOptions` applied on top — a `Some` domain replaces the resolved one, `None` keeps it, and a value above `DOMAIN_ID_MAX` is `InitError::DomainIdOutOfRange` rather than a backend failure later (the #206 rule).

ADOPT-BOUNDED, and the envelope is `rust:InitOptions`'s: the options object carries the one field rclrs's does (`domain_id`), so the call a tutorial writes ports unchanged, while any option rclrs grows later is absent here and the compiler says so. Same platform constraint as `rust:Context::default_from_env` — freestanding, the base it overrides is the BAKED context, stated on the type. Tests: `from_env_honours_the_domain_override`, `from_env_with_no_override_keeps_the_env_value`, `from_env_rejects_an_out_of_range_override` (hosted, `--features env,std`); `freestanding_default_from_env_is_the_bake` (`--features alloc`).

History: `declined` + `absent` (phase-428 Q1: the domain arrived through the boot-config ladder, not an options object); surveyed and kept by the phase-428 closure; decided 2026-09-07 (RFC-0089 "Context and `init`, settled") and landed.

issue 1637 (2026-10-05) — ENVELOPE WRITTEN where a porting user reads it: the method's rustdoc stated only the override rule; it now states the one-option `InitOptions`, the `DomainIdOutOfRange` refusal and the freestanding BAKED base.

envelope.text: Bounded: [`InitOptions`] carries rclrs's one option, `domain_id`, and no
a freestanding image has no argv, so the name is absent there

rust:Context::new.why:
phase-427 W9 (2026-09-07) — LANDED. `Context::new(args: impl IntoIterator<Item = impl AsRef<str>>, options: InitOptions) -> Result<Context, InitError>` (`packages/api/nros/src/init.rs:293`), HOSTED ONLY (`#[cfg(feature = "env")]`): `Context::new(std::env::args(), InitOptions::new())` compiles as written (`AsRef<str>` is a superset of rclrs's `Item = String`; `context_new_accepts_rclrs_argv_shape`).

ADOPT-BOUNDED, two bounds, both stated in the doc comment. (1) The PLATFORM CONSTRAINT: a freestanding image has no argv, so the name is ABSENT there and the compiler says so — `no function or associated item named new`; the constructors that exist on every target are `default_from_env` / `from_env`. (2) The argument contract: rclrs PARSES `--ros-args` (remaps, parameter overrides); ours does not parse them and does not silently drop them either. The refusal is the RUNTIME refuse-loud site: `packages/api/nros/src/init.rs:298` calls `refuse_ros_args` (`:464-471`, the ONE site shared with `init_with_args`), which scans with `args_have_ros_args` (`:451`, exact match) and on a hit logs `REFUSE_INIT_ARGS` (`:433`) through `nros_log` and panics with the same text — the shape `rclcpp::init(argc, argv)` has in `nros.hpp`. A vector with no ROS arguments passes through to `from_env(options)` untouched, because nothing was dropped. Tests: `context_new_refuses_ros_args` (`#[should_panic(expected = "--ros-args")]`), `context_new_passes_plain_args_through`.

Not `refuse-loud` as the disposition, deliberately: that word is for a name that EXISTS ONLY to refuse. This name works — with default options, with a domain override, with a plain argv — and refuses one VALUE; the value-level refusal is what `adopt-bounded`'s envelope carries, and the parse of `--ros-args` is still owed beside `nros::resolve_name` (RFC-0020 class 4), recorded on `rust:init_with_args`.

History: `gap` + `absent` (phase-428 Q1, then kept by the closure survey, which found it is not a `rename` of `init_with_args`); decided 2026-09-07 (RFC-0089 "Context and `init`, settled") and landed.

phase-467 Row 11 (2026-10-03) -- bound (2) CHANGED: it now PARSES. `-r`/`--remap` rules inside `--ros-args` are honoured (carried on the `Context`, installed by `create_executor{,_in}` as the fallback remap tier, launch rules win); every other ROS argument is refused loudly with the argument named. One parse shared with `init_with_args` (`parse_ros_args_or_refuse`), pinned equal by `context_new_parses_exactly_like_init_with_args`. `context_new_refuses_ros_args` became `context_new_refuses_what_it_cannot_honour` (`--enclave`), because refusing `-r` is no longer the contract. The full envelope is on `rust:init_with_args`, which also carries the one residue both names share -- `-p` parameter overrides, still refused -- as its `owed` witness. This row stays `divergence` because its OTHER bound (no argv on a freestanding image) is the platform constraint it was filed for.

rust:Context::ok.why: phase-428 Q1 follow-through (2026-09-06) — `rclrs::Context::ok(&self) -> bool`: whether the rcl context is still valid, i.e. `shutdown` has not been called on it. Our `Context` is a resolved VALUE (`packages/api/nros/src/init.rs:85`) with no shutdown state to report; the thing that can stop being live is the session, and that is the executor's (`Executor::open` / its spin verbs return the failure, `rust:Executor::spin`). A method that always answered `true` would be the silent-disagreement RFC-0089 forbids, so there is none. Absent: `no method named ok`.

rust:Context::with_locator_override.why: phase-427 W9 (2026-09-07) — `Context::with_locator_override(self, Option<&str>) -> Self` (`packages/api/nros/src/init.rs:364`): replace the locator with one handed in at RUN time when there is one; `None` or an empty string keeps the baked value. It exists for #166 / phase-286 W1 — native_sim test parallelism: the harness launches an image with `-testargs --nros-locator=<loc>` and a per-test router on that ephemeral port, and `nros_runtime_locator_override()` (`nros-platform-zephyr`, argv-backed) hands it back. The hook is an `extern "C"` only a Zephyr image defines, so it is resolved in the entry macros (`nros::zephyr_component_main!`, `nros::main!`'s Zephyr arm) and the result is handed to the context here, after `Context::default_from_env()`; on real hardware the hook returns NULL and the bake stands. No upstream counterpart: rclrs reads a process environment the launcher already set, which is what this override stands in for on a target that has none. See `rust:Context::baked`.

Implements `core::error::Error`. Visible since `env` joined the measured feature set.

phase-427 W9 (2026-09-07) — LANDED. No longer "the error type of the HOSTED init surface": it compiles on every target, and `impl core::error::Error` is ungated (the trait is `core`'s since 1.81). Gained `DomainIdOutOfRange` (`packages/api/nros/src/init.rs:104`): a domain above `DOMAIN_ID_MAX` from the environment, the bake, or an `InitOptions::with_domain_id` override — the hosted resolver's `DomainIdRange` used to fold into `EnvParseFailed`, which named the wrong failure. `EnvParseFailed` also covers a non-numeric baked `NROS_DOMAIN_ID` freestanding.

phase-427 W10 (2026-09-08) — LANDED. Two variants, both for the executor factories `Context::create_executor` / `create_executor_in`. `ExecutorOpenFailed(NodeError)` CARRIES the backend's own error rather than flattening it: "no RMW backend is registered" and "the router is not there" arrive as `Transport(InvalidConfig)` and `Transport(ConnectionFailed)` and want different fixes — issue 0465 is what collapsing them cost the last time. `BackingTooSmall { needed, given }` is the safe wrapper's refusal when a caller-supplied backing is shorter than the executor's tables need; it names BOTH numbers, because "too small" without them is not actionable, and it fires BEFORE the RMW is consulted so a short `static` is never reported as a missing router. This is still not rclrs's `RclrsError` — see `rust:RclrsError` — but it is now the same SHAPE of answer: a value naming the layer that failed.

phase-427 W9 (2026-09-07) — LANDED. `struct InitOptions { domain_id: Option<u32> }` (`packages/api/nros/src/init.rs:182`) with `new()`, `Default`, `with_domain_id(self, Option<usize>) -> Self` (`:199`, rclrs's signature — `usize` there; a value above `u32::MAX` saturates and the consuming constructor refuses it as `DomainIdOutOfRange`, since a builder has no `Result` to carry the refusal) its in-place twin `set_domain_id(&mut self, Option<usize>)` (`:204`, which the first parity run reported as the one theirs-only member of a type that now correlates `same`) and a `domain_id()` accessor. ADOPT-BOUNDED: rclrs's `InitOptions` has exactly this one field today, so the adoption is complete against the current upstream; the bound is that this is the ONLY option there will be here — a hosted-only option rclrs might add (anything that names the rcl allocator or the argv parse) is absent, and `with_domain_id` is the one setter upstream tutorials use. The platform constraint is the one on the constructors that consume it: freestanding, the override lands on the BAKED context. Test: `init_options_default_overrides_nothing` (`--features alloc`).

History: `divergence` / `theirs-only` ("the domain arrives through the boot-config ladder, not a mutable options object"), decided 2026-09-07 (RFC-0089 "Context and `init`, settled") and landed.

phase-467 — `domain_id()` returns `Option<usize>` now, which is rclrs's type and the type `with_domain_id` / `set_domain_id` already took. It returned `Option<u32>`, the STORED width, so the two setters spoke rclrs and the getter spoke the field; the closed `rust:Context::domain_id` row cited all three as already speaking `usize` and was two thirds right, which is why the inconsistency it argued FROM had to be fixed in the same pass rather than displaced onto `Context`. The saturation is unchanged and lives in the stored `u32`: a round trip through `u32::MAX + 1` still reports `u32::MAX`, and the refusal still lands on the consuming constructor as `DomainIdOutOfRange`, which is the one place with a `Result` to carry it. rust:OnSetContext.why: Two machine words of caller context, carried verbatim to an `OnSetParameterFn`. TWO because a C or C++ registration is a FUNCTION POINTER plus a user `void*`: one word would force each wrapper to keep a static side table mapping an index back to the pair, which is a second registry with its own bound. `usize` rather than `*mut c_void` because a raw pointer in that struct strips `ParameterServer`'s auto traits and the store lives inside the executor. Upstream has no correspondent — a closure captures. phase-417 W4.a.

owed.what: parameter overrides inside `--ros-args` (`-p`/`--param`/`--params-file`); the call refuses them by name, while `-r`/`--remap` is honoured

rust:init_with_args.why:
phase-467 Row 11 (2026-10-03) -- THE PARSE LANDED, and the row stays `gap` for exactly ONE residue: parameter overrides (`-p`/`--param`/`--params-file`), recorded in `owed` with a witness. Everything the row owed before -- the `--ros-args` parse, and the `-r`/`--remap` remap rules it carries -- is shipped. One parse (`parse_ros_args_or_refuse`, `packages/api/nros/src/init.rs`) serves this name and its twin `rust:Context::new`.

WHY STILL `gap` AND NOT `divergence`. SCHEMA.md (issue 1463): "a behaviour bound that is PERMANENT is not a `gap` at all -- it is a `divergence` with its constraint." The `-p` refusal is NOT permanent: RFC-0015 section 9 designs the runtime-parameter channel and its section 9.6 is open, and when it lands this parser is its POSIX producer. Calling the row closed while a porting user's `-p foo:=42` is still refused would be the stale closure 1463 was filed about. The OTHER bounds below ARE permanent (identity remaps: build-time freeze, RFC-0046; freestanding: no argv), and would make the row a `divergence` on their own once `-p` lands.

UPSTREAM'S CONTRACT: `rclcpp::init(argc, argv)` / rclrs `Context::new(args, ..)` hand the process arguments to `rcl_parse_arguments` (Humble `rcl/arguments.h`): ROS arguments between `--ros-args` and `--` (or the end), several scopes allowed, `-r`/`--remap [node:]from:=to` rules kept in argv order, `-p`/`--param` overrides, and rclcpp throws `UnknownROSArgsError` for any ROS argument rcl left unparsed. rclrs has no free `init_with_args`; this name is ours (the C++-symmetric anchor beside `init()`), so the key correlates `ours-only`.

OURS: `init_with_args(args)` parses with rcl's grammar (`nros_node::ros_args::parse_ros_args`, `packages/core/nros-node/src/ros_args.rs`) and returns a `Context` carrying the `-r` rules in a private field. `Context::create_executor` / `create_executor_in` install them in the executor's remap table tagged as the FALLBACK tier of `nros_node::names::resolve_name_layered` (PR #1523). From there they reach entities on every road that resolves names: `Executor::resolve_entity_name_for` (the C and C++ APIs), `ExecutorSink::create_entity` (`nros::node!` components, via `nros_node::ros_args::argv_fallback`), and the handle `Executor::create_node` returns -- which before this consulted NO remap at all, so a rule declared on the executor already missed every entity created through it.

THE PRECEDENCE RULE, decided by PR #1523 and now exercised with a real producer: LAUNCH IS AUTHORITATIVE; an argv rule applies only to a name the launch projected no rule for. RFC-0046's ruling for node identity, applied to remaps -- and rcl's own arrangement: `rcl_remap_topic_name` checks a node's LOCAL arguments (how launch and component containers hand a node its rules) and only on no match the GLOBAL ones `rcl_init` received (Humble `rcl/remap.h`). Within argv, the first rule wins (`foo:=bar bar:=baz` sends `foo` to `bar`), as rcl documents.

ADOPT-BOUNDED -- THE ENVELOPE, stated in the doc comment. Everything below is REFUSED LOUDLY at the call (logged through `nros_log`, then a panic carrying `REFUSE_INIT_ARGS` and the offending argument), never skipped:
  * `-p` / `--param` / `--params-file` -- THE OWED RESIDUE (see `owed`). Not built here because RFC-0015 section 9 owns the runtime-parameter channel (`nros_runtime_args_get`, `apply_runtime_param_overrides`, "writes into the same parameter store that ~/set_parameters reads") and its section 9.6 is still open; a second answer built on this row would pre-empt that RFC. It also does not fit this carrier: a remap is consulted when an entity is NAMED, a parameter override when a parameter is DECLARED, into a store that is image-wide (#1408) and would need its own executor table and sizing. When section 9 lands, `-p` is that channel's POSIX producer, using this parser, and this row becomes a `divergence`.
  * Node-identity remaps (`__node`, `__name`, `__ns`, any `__` rule). PLATFORM CONSTRAINT: an image's node identity is frozen at build time (RFC-0015 section 2.1) and launch-authoritative (RFC-0046), which has no argv rung.
  * `rostopic://` / `rosservice://` rules (rcl's own header marks them unfinished), `-e`/`--enclave`, the log flags, and any token inside a scope that is not a ROS flag.
  * The FREESTANDING half: the name is `cfg(feature = "env")`, absent on an image with no argv.

WHERE THE RULES DO NOT REACH, measured and stated rather than discovered: (1) `Context::config` cannot carry them into the `ExecutorConfig` `Executor::open` takes, so it REFUSES a context that has any (`config_refuses_a_context_that_carries_remaps`). (2) Entities registered through the executor's own `add_*` methods or a `node_mut` context are not remapped, because those are also where the C ABI and the component sink hand ALREADY-RESOLVED names -- remapping there would apply a rule twice, and `a:=b b:=c` would then send `a` to `c`, which rcl forbids. Splitting the user-facing entry from the post-resolution sink is the follow-up that would close (2). (3) A `nros sync` image reads no argv: its entry builds its own `RuntimeCtx` and never reaches `init_with_args`, consistent with RFC-0015 section 9.2, which classes topic remaps as graph topology for exactly those images.

TESTS. Parser: 10 in `ros_args.rs` (scopes, both flag spellings, node prefix, refusals by name). Chain -- real argv, parsed, installed, resolved: `a_launch_rule_wins_over_argv_even_when_argv_was_installed_first` (declaration order argues for the wrong winner), `an_argv_rule_applies_where_the_launch_projected_none`, `a_node_prefixed_argv_rule_reaches_only_that_node`, `within_argv_the_first_rule_wins`, `argv_fallback_yields_only_argv_rules_for_the_named_node`, `install_is_all_or_nothing`. NodeHandle, asserted on the name the BACKEND received: `create_node_handle_applies_an_argv_remap`, `create_node_handle_prefers_a_launch_rule_over_argv`, `create_node_handle_passes_an_unmatched_name_through_unchanged`. Context: `remap_rules_ride_on_the_context_in_argv_order`, `parameter_overrides_are_still_refused_by_name`, `identity_remaps_are_refused`, `context_new_parses_exactly_like_init_with_args`. Mutation-checked: dropping the fallback tier from the C/C++ resolver fails 3; flattening the table to first-match regardless of tier fails 3; making the handle consult no remap fails 2.

HISTORY. Recorded `gap` + `refuse-loud` from phase-427 W9, when the parameter was `_args` and `--ros-args -p foo:=42` had been silently discarded; re-dispositioned `adopt-bounded` on 2026-09-23 to match its twin. phase-467's study asked whether argv remaps should override launch-projected ones; PR #1317 measured that launch remaps are never projected into the environment at all (they are emitted into the generated entry), and PR #1523 landed the two-tier resolution and the precedence rule with an empty fallback, correcting the study's prescription, which had named the C/C++ store as if it were the only one.

rust:init_with_launch.why:
phase-428 W5 (2026-09-06) — ledgering a recorded sweep finding. RANKED-11, second of three. NO DISPOSITION IS WRITTEN. The four dispositions are what clause 1 does to a CANDIDATE FROM CLAUSE 2 (RFC-0089); this item has no upstream candidate, so there is nothing for a constraint to permit, weaken or refuse. — rclrs has no launch-model entry point; the C++ twins are `cpp:init_with_launch` / `cpp:init_with_launch_auto` in the node stage, and this row is their missing Rust counterpart as well as the finding.

THE FINDING: `packages/api/nros/src/init.rs:228` checks that the path EXISTS (`if !p.exists() { return Err(InitError::LaunchFileNotFound) }`) and then calls `read_env_context(ContextSource::Launch)`. It never parses the file. The returned `Context` reports `source == Launch`, so introspection CONFIRMS that the launch file was honoured when only its existence was.

HOW A USER FINDS OUT: SILENTLY WRONG, and the diagnostic actively misleads — a well-formed launch file with the wrong contents and an empty file that happens to exist produce identical, successful results. RFC-0046 makes launch authoritative for node identity, which is precisely why an unparsed one must not report `Launch`. The honest intermediate state is to report the source we actually used, or to refuse at the call naming the unparsed file. Re-verified by hand against the current worktree before this row was written.

rust:init_with_launch_auto.why:
phase-428 W5 (2026-09-06) — ledgering a recorded sweep finding. RANKED-11, third of three, and the emptier of the pair. NO DISPOSITION IS WRITTEN. The four dispositions are what clause 1 does to a CANDIDATE FROM CLAUSE 2 (RFC-0089); this item has no upstream candidate, so there is nothing for a constraint to permit, weaken or refuse.

`packages/api/nros/src/init.rs:212` is `read_env_context(ContextSource::Launch)` with NO path resolution at all — the three-step bringup resolution its own doc describes is marked "(NOT yet consumed; placeholder)". It returns a `Context` whose source says `Launch`. SILENTLY WRONG, for the same reason and with the same remedy as `rust:init_with_launch`; see that row. Both are `#[cfg(feature = "env")]`.
